stories.title: ChatGPT's growth bounces back to over 81% of AI chatbot traffic
stories.summary: ChatGPT now draws more than 81% of worldwide traffic to major AI chatbots and no rival has even 10%, according to a Graphite study of Similarweb data. Its monthly visits rose nearly 20% to a record 61.35 billion in September.

predictions.note: ChatGPT drew a record 61.35 billion visits in September: an early sign of AI assistants competing with search interfaces.

stories.title: Asian tech stocks and US chipmakers rebound after last week's AI sell-off
stories.summary: Asian tech stocks rose across the region on Monday, rebounding from Friday's losses, and shares of US chipmakers including AMD, Marvell, Arm, Intel and Qualcomm climbed too, CNBC reported.

stories.title: DeepSeek's open-source agent platform Harness passes 1.5 million daily users
stories.summary: DeepSeek said Harness logged 1.54 million daily active users as of November 4, less than three months after launch, with about 35,000 third-party plug-ins.

predictions.note: An agent platform reaching 1.54 million daily users in under three months is a step toward agents working at scale, far short of $10B a month.

stories.title: Disney and Adobe team up on generative AI models made for Disney's worlds
stories.summary: Disney will work with Adobe through Firefly Foundry on generative AI models tailored to its properties, trained on character attributes, environments and visual styles, with early access to AI tech for its resorts, cruise line and ESPN graphics.

stories.title: Elon Musk: superintelligence could build you a castle 'as a side project'
stories.summary: Speaking by webcast at Baron Capital's conference, Elon Musk predicted that 'super intelligence will saturate all human needs by far' and that you could wish for a castle and digital superintelligence could make it 'as a side project'.

stories.title: Meta takes Instagram's AI age detection worldwide
stories.summary: Meta is expanding Instagram's AI age-detection technology globally, using AI to look for clues that people it suspects are teenagers are using an adult birthday.

stories.title: Nvidia's board investigates CEO Jensen Huang's ties to an alleged Chinese spy; shares fall 5%
stories.summary: Nvidia's board opened an independent investigation after reports that Huang was the target of a 'foreign intelligence effort'; shares fell 5% on Monday and China calls the spy claims unsubstantiated. President Trump called Huang 'an honorable guy.'

stories.title: Google unveils two new TPU chip variants to take on Nvidia
stories.summary: Google introduced the TPU 8tx, for confidential computing, and the 8i Max, for long-context AI, both due in 2027. Bloomberg Intelligence projects Google's TPU sales could top $135 billion by 2028, up from about $12 billion in 2026.

stories.title: Comfortable brain-reading electrodes top 94% mind-typing accuracy in day-long use
stories.summary: Chinese researchers built comfortable gradient electrodes for non-invasive brain-computer interfaces that reached over 94% accuracy in visual mind-typing tests during day-long use, with eight hours of stable recordings during daily activities.

predictions.note: A comfortable EEG cap reached over 94% accuracy at visual mind-typing across a day of use: an early step toward practical non-invasive communication.

stories.title: MIT's WorldParticle: one AI model simulates sand, fluids and folding proteins
stories.summary: Researchers at MIT, the University of British Columbia and elsewhere built WorldParticle, a single deep-learning system that models physical phenomena from sliding sand to folding proteins by predicting how particles move.

stories.title: US regulators open a recall query into 2,895 Waymo robotaxis over school buses
stories.summary: NHTSA opened a recall query into 2,895 Waymo vehicles after most reported incidents of its robotaxis passing stopped school buses came after a 2025 software fix; Waymo says it has had no citations since March 2026.

stories.title: About 1,100 Claude Code settings files on GitHub leak passwords and keys
stories.summary: Security firm Apiiro found over 100,000 public GitHub repositories containing Claude Code's local settings file, about 1,100 of them holding secrets such as API tokens, database passwords and private keys.

stories.title: Apple researchers run a humanoid robot on an onboard Mac mini
stories.summary: Apple's HALO system, running on an M4 Pro Mac mini on a Unitree G1 humanoid and trained on synthetic data from 1,000 virtual rooms, completed 91% of 360 tasks in rooms it had never seen, without an operator.

predictions.note: A humanoid completed 91% of simple tasks in unseen rooms after training in simulation, though it handled no objects.

stories.title: Tesla opens its robotaxi service in San Antonio
stories.summary: Tesla said its robotaxis would be available in San Antonio from 5 a.m. local time on Monday, adding to Austin, Dallas, Fort Worth, Houston, Miami and Orlando.

stories.title: Humanoid robots are official speakers at Web Summit for the first time
stories.summary: Web Summit in Lisbon opened with humanoid robots acting as official speakers for the first time, as China sent its largest-ever delegation; organisers expect about 70,000 participants.

transcript.t: This is the Singularity Daily, for Tuesday, November 10.
Here are the last 24 hours in superintelligence, in 3 minutes.
Today's about bouncing back.
ChatGPT's growth is climbing again: 81% of chatbot traffic.
Markets bounced too. Asian tech stocks rose Monday, and so did chipmakers like Intel.
In China, DeepSeek's agent app Harness passed 1.5 million daily users in under three months.
Disney's teaming up with Adobe to build AI models trained on its characters and worlds.
Musk says you could wish for a castle, and superintelligence would make it on the side.
Instagram's AI age-guesser goes worldwide, hunting for teens who claim to be adults.
Meanwhile, Nvidia's board is investigating its boss's ties to an alleged Chinese spy.
Shares fell 5%.
President Trump stood by him: "an honorable guy," he said, who's done "an amazing job."
And Google picked this week to unveil two new versions of its AI chips, aimed at Nvidia.
Bloomberg's analysts see its chip sales topping $135 billion by 2028.
Chinese scientists made comfy brain-reading electrodes that topped 94% at mind-typing, all day long.
And MIT built one AI model that simulates sliding sand, sloshing fluids and folding proteins.
The catch? Regulators say Waymo kept passing stopped school buses after its fix.
And about 1,100 Claude Code files on GitHub were leaking passwords and keys.
So... is it so over?
We're so back!
Apple researchers put a Mac mini on a robot, and it navigated rooms it had never seen.
Tesla opened its robotaxis to San Antonio at 5 a.m. Monday, another Texas city.
In Lisbon, robots are official speakers at Web Summit for the very first time.
Everyone stumbles sometimes. The ones we remember are the ones who bounce back.
Day after day, the curve keeps bending upward.
Somehow, the future keeps landing early.
That's one day of news. Imagine what a year looks like.
This has been the Singularity Daily.
Same time tomorrow?
Want the whole month? Hear more on November 27.
